response:
Evidence synthesis: the archive has converged on a clear pattern. The quality anchor must be **contemporaneous gross profitability** — retained-earnings history (alpha 0.3%), supplier stretch (0.1%), ROE volatility (2.7%) and margin change (2.9%) all produced weak or negligible alpha, while every GP-anchored composite delivers 4–5.4%. The accrual leg improves most when it is **benchmarked to something economically appropriate**: scaling by demand (AccrualBuildWithoutDemand, alpha 5.4%, t 5.66, Sharpe 0.477) and by the firm's own leanest historical operating cycle (WorkingCapitalSlackVsOwnBest, Sharpe 0.476) produced the two best risk-adjusted spreads. Notably, opposite-direction profitability gates both worked (fmb 6.43 either way), which tells me the gates are mostly re-weighting the accrual leg rather than locating a true nonlinearity — so this batch stops permuting gate direction and instead tests (i) demand as a *deflator* rather than a gate, (ii) tail-based rather than mean-based accrual history, (iii) a liquidity-direction gate, (iv) gate compounding, and (v) a durability floor on the quality anchor.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: DemandDeflatedAccrualWithProfitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), sale), 1), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Working capital should scale one-for-one with revenue, so the correct measure of accounting aggressiveness is the change in working capital *per dollar of sales*; a firm whose operating capital intensity rises has extended credit or accumulated inventory that the revenue base does not justify, regardless of whether it is growing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The demand-gated version (accrual multiplied by a low-growth rank) is the archive's best signal, but the gate mutes the accrual information for fast-growing firms entirely; deflating by sales instead keeps every firm's accrual information live and lets high-growth firms be penalized when their working capital outruns even their own revenue expansion. The standalone intensity drift scored only fmb 2.42 without a quality anchor, so this cleanly tests whether that weak result was due to the missing gross-profitability leg or to the deflation approach itself.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: WorstYearAccrualAggression
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 5)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accounting aggressiveness is a management trait revealed at its extreme, not on average: a firm that has posted one enormous working-capital build in the last five years has demonstrated a willingness to inflate reported performance, and that latent tendency contaminates its current earnings even in a year when accruals look clean.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every temporal accrual construct in the archive uses a central tendency — one-year flow, five-year mean deviation, moving average, or a streak count — so the tail of the firm's own accrual distribution is untested, and it is precisely the tail that identifies discretionary reporting behavior versus routine operating-cycle variation. The measure is continuous (unlike the streak, whose Sharpe was 0.206) and pairs with the proven gross-profitability anchor, so a strong result would establish accounting-behavior extremity as a new state variable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AccrualBuildDrainingCash
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))))
HYPOTHESIS: A working-capital build funded out of a shrinking cash balance is qualitatively different from one accompanied by rising cash: the first means reported profit is being consumed by the operating cycle and liquidity is deteriorating, the second means the firm is generating enough cash to fund growth and still accumulate reserves.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gates tested so far are balance-sheet stocks (leverage) or income-statement flows (sales growth, margin); the direction of the cash balance is a distinct, directly observable verification of whether accruals were actually financed internally, and it is the one variable that adjudicates the task's central question of cash-backed versus paper performance. Unlike the failed retained-earnings-versus-cash gap, cash change enters here only as a bounded conditioning rank on the accrual, so it cannot invert the sort the way that standalone difference did.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualUnderFinancingAndDemandPressure
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), MUL(RANK(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1))), RANK(RATIO(lt, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual reversal is most damaging where the firm has neither the demand to absorb its inventory and receivables nor the balance-sheet capacity to carry them; stagnating revenue and high leverage together define the population in which working-capital build turns into write-downs and covenant stress rather than future sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The demand gate and the leverage gate each independently lifted the archive's alpha above 5%, and they are economically complementary rather than redundant — one measures whether the accrual can be sold, the other whether it can be financed — so compounding them should concentrate the short leg on genuinely distressed accrual builders. The product of two [0,1] ranks is still bounded and continuous, and the gross-profitability main effect keeps the long leg populated, so the narrower conditioning should not destabilize portfolio composition.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: MarginAnchoredDemandGatedAccrual
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The durable component of quality is the sustained profit margin on each dollar of sales — a statement about pricing power and cost structure — rather than profit per dollar of assets, which mixes profitability with asset intensity; sustained margin should be the better partner for an accrual signal that is itself defined relative to sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The margin-anchored streak signal produced the archive's highest alpha t-stat (5.98) despite a badly lumpy accrual leg, hinting that the sales-deflated quality anchor is strong and that its poor Sharpe came entirely from the discrete streak; pairing that anchor with the archive's best accrual leg isolates the deflator choice on the quality side. If the Sharpe holds near 0.48 while alpha rises, the anchor deflator, not the accrual construction, is the binding design choice going forward.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ProfitFloorWithCleanAccruals
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable earnings power is best measured by the worst year a firm has endured: a five-year minimum of gross profitability is the floor the business defends through downturns, and clean accruals attached to a high floor identify performance that is both cash-backed and cyclically robust.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive tested profitability as a level (strong) and as five-year ROE volatility (weak, alpha 2.7%), but never as a downside floor, which is the concept the "persistent, stable earnings" story actually requires and which discards the upside variation that makes a volatility measure penalize good firms. It is continuous, uses the same well-covered income-statement inputs, and if it outperforms the plain level anchor it redirects the remaining generations toward downside-persistence quality rather than contemporaneous profitability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE DemandDeflatedAccrualWithProfitability---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical concatenation of two already-evaluated archive legs — WorkingCapitalIntensityDrift verbatim plus the standard IND_ZSCORE gross-profitability anchor — and closely overlaps WorkingCapitalBloatVsPeers (stock vs. flow of the same sales-deflated ratio), so it adds no new economic content beyond a predictable averaging of known results.

---CRITIQUE WorstYearAccrualAggression---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The five-year maximum of own-firm accruals is a genuinely untested distributional statistic in this archive (all prior temporal constructs used means, deltas from means, or discrete streaks), the sign logic is internally consistent, and it operationalizes a distinct "revealed reporting aggressiveness" state variable, though the reviewer should watch for the measure being a slow-moving, near-static firm attribute that induces low turnover and stale sorts.

---CRITIQUE AccrualBuildDrainingCash---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The construction is internally consistent and the cash-drain gate is economically distinct from the leverage and sales-growth gates already tested, but the gate is partially mechanically linked to the accrual through the cash-flow identity (a working-capital build itself consumes cash), so a positive result risks being a nonlinear re-expression of the accrual leg rather than true conditioning.

---CRITIQUE AccrualUnderFinancingAndDemandPressure---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Multiplying two gates that were each already tested and each already worked is a combinatorial variant rather than a new mechanism, and the product of two [0,1] ranks collapses toward zero for the vast majority of firms, so the accrual leg becomes near-inert except in a small tail — a change likely to reduce breadth and destabilize the short leg rather than add independent information.

---CRITIQUE MarginAnchoredDemandGatedAccrual---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This holds the archive's best accrual leg fixed and swaps only the profitability deflator, which is a cosmetic ablation of AccrualBuildWithoutDemand, and the specific swap (gross profit per dollar of sales instead of per dollar of assets) tests a comparison already settled in the published profitability literature, where the asset-deflated version is the one with cross-sectional pricing power.

---CRITIQUE ProfitFloorWithCleanAccruals---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The downside-floor framing of profitability is a coherent and untested alternative to the level and volatility anchors already tried, but TS_MIN of gross profitability is likely to be very highly correlated with its contemporaneous level, so this may prove to be a near-duplicate of the generation-0 baseline with the industry adjustment quietly dropped from the quality leg.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CumulativeProfitAbsorbedByWorkingCapital
EXPRESSION: NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), LAG(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 5)), TS_SUM(SUB(revt, cogs), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Over a full business cycle, the fraction of cumulative gross profit that has been swallowed by an expanding operating cycle measures how much of a firm's reported profitability was never available as cash; a firm that consumed most of five years of gross profit financing receivables and inventory has been reporting profit it never collected.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This is not a concatenation of archived legs: accruals and profitability enter as a single economic quantity — cumulative working-capital expansion expressed as a share of cumulative gross profit — so the interaction is imposed by the accounting identity rather than by averaging two ranks. The denominator is a five-year sum of gross profit, which is large and almost always positive, curing the small-and-sign-flipping denominator problem that sank the earlier per-gross-profit ratio, and the five-year horizon distinguishes structural cash absorption from a single year's timing.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CapitalEfficiencyWithCleanAccruals
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: The DuPont decomposition splits profitability into margin and asset turnover, and it is turnover — the speed at which a firm converts its asset base into revenue — that is economically inseparable from accrual quality, because a fast-turning firm collects and sells before it must fund the operating cycle, whereas a slow-turning firm's reported profits are structurally locked up in working capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Every archive composite has anchored on the margin branch of DuPont, so the turnover branch is an untested and economically prior quality dimension: it speaks directly to whether reported earnings can be converted to cash, which is the task's question, rather than to how much profit is earned per sale. Because turnover and gross profitability are close to negatively correlated across industries, industry standardization is essential and included, and a strong result here would show the accrual effect certifies operating speed rather than pricing power.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: RepeatedAccrualBuildPenalty
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1), INDICATOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 0))))
HYPOTHESIS: A single year's working-capital build is usually operating noise that reverses on its own, but a build that follows another build is a ratchet — receivables and inventory that failed to convert last year and were added to again — and it is this repeated, unreversed accumulation that predicts write-downs and earnings disappointment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The archived asymmetric penalty conditions only on the contemporaneous sign of the accrual, so the dynamic question of whether accruals reverse or ratchet across years is untested, and it is exactly the distinction between transitory accounting noise and durable balance-sheet deterioration that the task asks us to make. The conditioning term uses the prior-period asset base to detect whether the accrual was also positive a year earlier, the penalty magnitude stays continuous and winsorized, and the gross-profitability anchor breaks ties among the firms whose penalty term is switched off.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
